saints.name: St. John Bosco
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: The apostle of youth in industrial Turin, who founded the Salesians and taught by kindness rather than punishment…
biography: Born on 16 August 1815 at the hamlet of Becchi near Castelnuovo d'Asti, John lost his father at the age of two and was raised in poverty by his mother Margaret. A dream at nine, bidding him win wild boys by gentleness rather than blows, never left him. Ordained at Turin in 1841, he gave himself to the abandoned youth of that industrial city.

Meeting a young bricklayer, Bartholomew Garelli, in a sacristy on the feast of the Immaculate Conception in 1841, he began gathering street boys into a Sunday oratory, adding workshops, schools, and lodgings that in time sheltered hundreds. His 'preventive system' of education rested on reason, religion, and loving-kindness rather than punishment.

In 1859 he formed his helpers into the Society of St. Francis de Sales, the Salesians, and with Mary Mazzarello founded the Daughters of Mary Help of Christians for girls. His print-shops, where boys learned the trade, made him a patron of editors and publishers. He died at Turin on 31 January 1888 and was canonized on Easter Sunday 1934 by Pius XI, who had known him.
saints.knownFor: Educating poor youth by the “preventive system” of loving-kindness.
